comparator.academicYear: Indicative 2027–2028 year 1, 2028–2029 year 2 and 2029–2030 year 3 prospectus pathway
comparator.sourceNotes: The coherent non-abroad pathway has twelve compulsory 5-EC first-year courses (60 EC). Two 0-EC academic support activities are excluded from the 180-EC total. In year two, six required 5-EC courses total 30 EC, with 30 EC of restricted Faculty of Arts minor choices (two 15-EC minors); additional English language/culture minors are optional rather than required. In year three, the non-abroad pathway consists of four compulsory 5-EC courses, a required 10-EC bachelor thesis in literature or linguistics, and 30 EC of free electives. An abroad version is an alternative study arrangement and is not combined with the domestic version. These year pages are expressly indicative prospectus years and do not establish the final curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant.

programmes.label: English Language and Culture at Radboud University

exception.reason: The programme integrates sustained English proficiency, English phonetics, syntax, historical and world English linguistics, British and American literary history, specialist research and a required thesis. UCR has literature, stylistics, rhetoric and media courses taught in English, but lacks dedicated English-language proficiency and phonology/syntax teaching and the multi-period English literature and linguistics sequence. Filling a 24-course closest match with general literature, history, art and media courses would misrepresent those gaps as English Studies training.
exception.curriculumContext: The public 2027–2028, 2028–2029 and 2029–2030 year-specific pages are provisional prospective-student pathways. The year-three comparison instantiates the non-abroad option, preserving its actual free electives and compulsory thesis.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (151 course rows), including profiles, descriptions, prerequisites and planned semester offerings. MCCLITR111/112/211/212/311/312 support general literary analysis and narrative; MCCCOMM111/211/213/311/312 support rhetoric, stylistics and communication; MCCMEDI211 treats American media and HCBCOGN312 psycholinguistics. These are meaningful adjacent studies, but the workbook has no sequence in English phonetics, phonology, syntax, historical English, English language proficiency or period-specific British and American literature. The nearest courses cannot sustain a defensible 24-course English Language and Culture closest match.
